sections.heading: Basic Attack - Stringblade
sections.text:
Press repeatedly or hold Normal Attack to perform up to 4 consecutive attacks, dealing Aero DMG .

 Basic Attack - Stringblade Stage 1 and Basic Attack - Stringblade Stage 4 are in Sheathed Stance.

 Basic Attack - Stringblade Stage 2 and Basic Attack - Stringblade Stage 3 are in Drawn Stance.

sections.heading: Heavy Attack - Stringblade
sections.text:
When Qin Heart and Sword Cadence are full, Heavy Attack - Stringblade becomes available.

 Hold Normal Attack to consume STA and cast this skill, dealing Aero DMG .

 Casting this skill consumes all Qin Heart and Sword Cadence and sends Qingxiao into the Ephemeral Transcendence state.

sections.heading: Mid-air Attack - Stringblade
sections.text:
Press Normal Attack consecutively or hold it down to perform up to 3 consecutive attacks, dealing Aero DMG .

 This skill is in Drawn Stance.

 After landing from Mid-air Attack - Stringblade Stage 3, press or hold Normal Attack within a certain time to cast Basic Attack - Stringblade Stage 3.

 While in mid-air, Resonance Skill is replaced by Mid-air Attack - Stringblade Stage 3.

sections.heading: Plunging Attack
sections.text:
While in the Sword Flight state, Jump is replaced by Plunging Attack.

 Consume STA to perform a Plunging Attack, dealing Aero DMG .

 While out of the Ephemeral Transcendence state, press Normal Attack within a certain time after casting this skill to cast Basic Attack - Stringblade Stage 3.

sections.heading: Dodge Counter - Stringblade
sections.text:
Press Normal Attack within a certain time after a successful Dodge to attack the target, dealing Aero DMG .

 This skill is in Drawn Stance.

 Press or hold Normal Attack within a certain time after casting this skill to cast Basic Attack - Stringblade Stage 4.

When Heart Sword Intent is full, Heavy Attack - Heaven's Reckoning: Ephemeral Transcendence becomes available. Hold Normal Attack to cast the skill, dealing Aero DMG .

sections.heading: Mindlock
sections.text:
Mindlock stacks up to 15 times.

 Each time when a Resonator in the team inflicts Tune Strain - Interfered on a target, inflict 1 stack of Mindlock on the target.

 For each stack of Mindlock on the target, DMG taken from Qingxiao's following skills is Amplified by 2% , with an additional 5% per stack for the first 7 stacks.
 Heavy Attack - Stringblade, Basic Attack - Ephemeral Transcendence, Dodge Counter - Ephemeral Transcendence, Heavy Attack - Heaven's Reckoning: Ephemeral Transcendence, Resonance Liberation - Billows Beneath Heaven.

sections.heading: Heaven's Clarity
sections.text:
Upon entering combat or casting Resonance Liberation Billows Beneath Heaven, gain Heaven's Clarity.

 When Sheathed Stance/Drawn Stance moves deal damage, the rates at which Qin Heart/Sword Cadence are obtained increase by 100% .

 When casting Heavy Attack - Stringblade, inflict 3 stacks of Mindlock on nearby targets, and enhance the next Heavy Attack - Heaven's Reckoning: Ephemeral Transcendence: its DMG Multiplier is increased by 100% and it builds additional Off-Tune Level on the target. Switching to another Resonator ends the Heavy Attack - Heaven's Reckoning: Ephemeral Transcendence enhancement.

 Casting Heavy Attack - Heaven's Reckoning: Ephemeral Transcendence removes Heaven's Clarity.

sections.heading: Swordlight Ward
sections.text:
Casting Intro Skill - Tonality Shift or Heavy Attack - Stringblade grants 1 stack of Swordlight Ward.

 Swordlight Ward stacks up to 1 time. When taking DMG from an enemy's attack, 1 stacks of Swordlight Ward can be consumed to grant immunity to interruption and reduce DMG taken by 60% for 1s . This effect can be triggered once per second.

sections.heading: Sword Flight
sections.text:
While in the Sword Flight state, Qingxiao moves with a special animation.

 Moving in Sword Flight continuously consumes Flight Qi.

 Casting the following skills sends Qingxiao into the Sword Flight state:
 Sword Dodge, Heavy Attack - Stringblade, Mid-air Attack - Stringblade Stage 1, Mid-air Attack - Stringblade Stage 2, Severing Note: Ascendant, Basic Attack - Ephemeral Transcendence, Dodge Counter - Ephemeral Transcendence, Heavy Attack - Heaven's Reckoning: Ephemeral Transcendence, and Intro Skill - Tonality Shift.

 Exit the Sword Flight state by
 Casting Mid-air Attack - Stringblade Stage 3 or Plunging Attack.

 Triggering certain environmental interactions or Utilities.

 Returning to the ground.

 Switching to another Resonator.

 Depleting all Flight Qi.

sections.heading: Sword Step
sections.text:
While in the Sword Flight state, hold Jump to leap up and dash forward a short distance.

 Sword Step can only be cast once during Sword Flight.

sections.heading: Pros
Cons
Review
sections.text: Qingxiao is a 5-star Aero Sword DPS character who plays into the Tune Strain archetype and mostly fights in mid-air, which makes her very reminiscent of the other Tune Strain DPS, Luuk Herssen, in that sense. Not only that, they share teammates and have a similar meta position, so they are overall quite easy to compare to each other. However, their playstyles differ drastically, so let’s cover her kit in more depth:

sections.heading: Rotation & Goals
sections.text:
Qingxiao’s rotation goal is to enter her “Ephemeral Transcendence” state to cast a special Heavy Attack called Heaven’s Reckoning that deals a ton of damage. Her main damage-dealing moves are her Ultimate, Heaven’s Reckoning, her base form Heavy Attack that allows her to enter her enhanced state, as well as her Outro. The idea is to chain those as quickly together as possible to complete a rotation.
 To do this, Basic Attacks will mostly be used, as well as a Skill called Severing Note: Judgement. The overwhelming majority of her rotation following an Intro can be simply completed by holding the Basic Attack down - you only change this up two times to cast her Skill and her Ultimate. That’s all. Her gameplay doesn’t get easier than this.

sections.heading: Other Key Mechanics
sections.text:
Qingxiao’s main mechanic is Tune Strain. Whenever she deals damage to an enemy once, she applies 1 stack of Tune Strain, which is converted into extra total damage to that target based on the amount of stacks when Tune Break Skills are cast. Having teammates that can apply extra stacks and cause faster Tune Break Skill casts to actually benefit from the stacks of Tune Strain applied on the enemy will prove key to increasing her overall damage output, particularly considering her Mindlock mechanic that amplifies damage of the overwhelming majority of her attacks based on the amount of Tune Strain applied on targets (7% for the first 7 stacks, 2% for the next 8, for a total of 65% possible DMG amplification).
 Additionally, she gains Interruption Immunity and 60% DMG taken reduction for 1 attack after her Intro or her base Heavy Attack, inflicts additional Mindlock on every base Heavy Attack (3 stacks) and when other characters apply Tune Strain (1 stack), and can apply Mindlock stats in multi-wave content.
 Lastly, in terms of Quickswap restrictions, Qingxiao should be free to build her Forte resources to cast her initial Heavy Attack before entering her Enhanced State, at which point the enhancements on her Heaven’s Reckoning Heavy Attack (extremely significant damage increases) get removed if you swap, so switching characters upon entering her enhanced state is discouraged. So building up to the initial Heavy Attack quicker by pre-building Forte resources is as optimized as you can go.
 Meta Position & Conclusion
 Overall, Qingxiao is at the top of the single-target metagame on her release, and it seems her Denia+Mornye team, which is her on-release best in slot, is there to stay as her intended best team. This means Qingxiao and Luuk share ideal teammates, so you have to privilege one or the other. And it’s a no-brainer who to pick if you have a Tune Strain team - Qingxiao’s base damage is simply higher, so she’s a stronger character overall. In the Aero department, however, Luuk has been known to face issues in Whimpering Wastes and he shares a playstyle with Qingxiao, being mid-air combat and Tune Strain. Sigrika on the other hand, Qingxiao’s rival in the Aero Main DPS department, has the best results of any character in Whimpering Wastes as of Qingxiao’s release. This calls into question Qingxiao’s value across endgame modes.
 Additionally, Qingxiao has a pretty significant reliance on either owning Denia and Mornye together specifically (trying to use Denia without Mornye results in major team DPS drop-offs, so there are no alternatives), or owning Lynae (at which point you can make do with ideally Mornye, but Ciaccona and Shorekeeper are fine enough alternatives as well). This, paired with a strong desire for her Signature weapon, makes Qingxiao quite the expensive character to get up and running. All this for a DPS who cannot cover all 3 endgame modes Wuthering Waves offers that efficiently, as remember she falls behind in Whimpering Wastes compared to her competition.
 In conclusion, Qingxiao is an extremely strong single-target pick, but we don’t lack those in the current Wuthering Waves meta. For how expensive Qingxiao is, she fails to deliver top-level performance across all 3 endgame modes, and requests particularly desirable teammates across other meta teams (mostly Aemeath and Luuk). She is without a doubt one of the strongest single-target damage dealer picks, but be mindful of her investment requirements as well as her performance in Whimpering Wastes before deciding whether to get her or not.

sections.text:
Qingxiao is likely the simplest Main DPS character to pilot in the history of the game: inputs-wise, you only need to hold Basic Attack for a while, press Skill, hold Basic Attack again for a while, press Ultimate, Echo and Outro. sections.heading: Additional Tips & Tricks
sections.text: It’s possible to build up Forte resources to work towards Heavy: Stringblade before her Intro in more quickswap-friendly compositions; however, Qingxiao doesn’t ideally play in team compositions with a lot of quickswap flexibility. This may result in minimal rotation time savings. Additionally, depending on your weapon choice and combat length, you may use her Ultimate later or earlier in her rotation at your discretion. Keep in mind it’s used at the latest point possible in the above example because you get to stack up her Signature Weapon’s passive to the max before unleashing it.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Lynae Denia - Qingxiao requires a Tune Strain Hybrid buffer to function at her best. If Mornye is accessible, Denia is the strongest to use as together they provide the best array of buffs possible for her. Otherwise, Lynae is a perfectly fine alternative ideally with Mornye as she also sports lots of generalist buffs and Tune Strain application, but will usually work better with alternative Support options such as Ciaccona and Shorekeeper as her buffs are less specialized.
 Mornye Ciaccona The Shorekeeper - Qingxiao's ideal Support option is evidently the only designated Tune Strain-related Support option Mornye, as she causes more Tune Strain to be applied quicker and provides lots of buffs for characters who interact with the mechanic. However, if Lynae is the Hybrid character that supports Qingxiao, she works best with Mornye but also makes good use of alternative Supports like Ciaccona and Shorekeeper, only having to deal with minimal team damage losses if Mornye is inaccessible/has to be replaced.

 Pros & Cons
 Pros
 High single-target damage output, up to par with the rest of modern 3.x characters;

 Has the ability to chase down airborne enemies with relative ease - rotation can stay consistent across boss encounters;

 Easiest DPS rotation in the game’s history - just hold left click for the majority of the time; the rotation practically completes itself.

 Cons
 One of the most restrictive modern characters when it comes to teambuilding. Needs either Denia+Mornye specifically, or Lynae + a strong premium support. Otherwise, will fall behind significantly compared to all modern DPS characters in the game;

 Faces issues in multiwave/AoE content because of gameplay revolving around Tune Strain and mid-air attacks, much like Luuk;

 “Here at Wuthering Waves, we strive to deliver an interactive gameplay experience to all players.”

 Review
 Qingxiao is a 5-star Aero Sword DPS character who plays into the Tune Strain archetype and mostly fights in mid-air, which makes her very reminiscent of the other Tune Strain DPS, Luuk Herssen, in that sense. Not only that, they share teammates and have a similar meta position, so they are overall quite easy to compare to each other. However, their playstyles differ drastically, so let’s cover her kit in more depth:
 Rotation & Goals
 Qingxiao’s rotation goal is to enter her “Ephemeral Transcendence” state to cast a special Heavy Attack called Heaven’s Reckoning that deals a ton of damage. Her main damage-dealing moves are her Ultimate, Heaven’s Reckoning, her base form Heavy Attack that allows her to enter her enhanced state, as well as her Outro. The idea is to chain those as quickly together as possible to complete a rotation.
 To do this, Basic Attacks will mostly be used, as well as a Skill called Severing Note: Judgement. The overwhelming majority of her rotation following an Intro can be simply completed by holding the Basic Attack down - you only change this up two times to cast her Skill and her Ultimate. That’s all. Her gameplay doesn’t get easier than this.
 Other Key Mechanics
 Qingxiao’s main mechanic is Tune Strain. Whenever she deals damage to an enemy once, she applies 1 stack of Tune Strain, which is converted into extra total damage to that target based on the amount of stacks when Tune Break Skills are cast. Having teammates that can apply extra stacks and cause faster Tune Break Skill casts to actually benefit from the stacks of Tune Strain applied on the enemy will prove key to increasing her overall damage output, particularly considering her Mindlock mechanic that amplifies damage of the overwhelming majority of her attacks based on the amount of Tune Strain applied on targets (7% for the first 7 stacks, 2% for the next 8, for a total of 65% possible DMG amplification).
 Additionally, she gains Interruption Immunity and 60% DMG taken reduction for 1 attack after her Intro or her base Heavy Attack, inflicts additional Mindlock on every base Heavy Attack (3 stacks) and when other characters apply Tune Strain (1 stack), and can apply Mindlock stats in multi-wave content.
 Lastly, in terms of Quickswap restrictions, Qingxiao should be free to build her Forte resources to cast her initial Heavy Attack before entering her Enhanced State, at which point the enhancements on her Heaven’s Reckoning Heavy Attack (extremely significant damage increases) get removed if you swap, so switching characters upon entering her enhanced state is discouraged. So building up to the initial Heavy Attack quicker by pre-building Forte resources is as optimized as you can go.
 Meta Position & Conclusion
 Overall, Qingxiao is at the top of the single-target metagame on her release, and it seems her Denia+Mornye team, which is her on-release best in slot, is there to stay as her intended best team. This means Qingxiao and Luuk share ideal teammates, so you have to privilege one or the other. And it’s a no-brainer who to pick if you have a Tune Strain team - Qingxiao’s base damage is simply higher, so she’s a stronger character overall. In the Aero department, however, Luuk has been known to face issues in Whimpering Wastes and he shares a playstyle with Qingxiao, being mid-air combat and Tune Strain. Sigrika on the other hand, Qingxiao’s rival in the Aero Main DPS department, has the best results of any character in Whimpering Wastes as of Qingxiao’s release. This calls into question Qingxiao’s value across endgame modes.
 Additionally, Qingxiao has a pretty significant reliance on either owning Denia and Mornye together specifically (trying to use Denia without Mornye results in major team DPS drop-offs, so there are no alternatives), or owning Lynae (at which point you can make do with ideally Mornye, but Ciaccona and Shorekeeper are fine enough alternatives as well). This, paired with a strong desire for her Signature weapon, makes Qingxiao quite the expensive character to get up and running. All this for a DPS who cannot cover all 3 endgame modes Wuthering Waves offers that efficiently, as remember she falls behind in Whimpering Wastes compared to her competition.
 In conclusion, Qingxiao is an extremely strong single-target pick, but we don’t lack those in the current Wuthering Waves meta. For how expensive Qingxiao is, she fails to deliver top-level performance across all 3 endgame modes, and requests particularly desirable teammates across other meta teams (mostly Aemeath and Luuk). She is without a doubt one of the strongest single-target damage dealer picks, but be mindful of her investment requirements as well as her performance in Whimpering Wastes before deciding whether to get her or not.

 Additional Tips & Tricks
 It’s possible to build up Forte resources to work towards Heavy: Stringblade before her Intro in more quickswap-friendly compositions; however, Qingxiao doesn’t ideally play in team compositions with a lot of quickswap flexibility. This may result in minimal rotation time savings. Additionally, depending on your weapon choice and combat length, you may use her Ultimate later or earlier in her rotation at your discretion. Keep in mind it’s used at the latest point possible in the above example because you get to stack up her Signature Weapon’s passive to the max before unleashing it.

 Synergies
 Lynae Denia - Qingxiao requires a Tune Strain Hybrid buffer to function at her best. If Mornye is accessible, Denia is the strongest to use as together they provide the best array of buffs possible for her. Otherwise, Lynae is a perfectly fine alternative ideally with Mornye as she also sports lots of generalist buffs and Tune Strain application, but will usually work better with alternative Support options such as Ciaccona and Shorekeeper as her buffs are less specialized.
 Mornye Ciaccona The Shorekeeper - Qingxiao's ideal Support option is evidently the only designated Tune Strain-related Support option Mornye, as she causes more Tune Strain to be applied quicker and provides lots of buffs for characters who interact with the mechanic. However, if Lynae is the Hybrid character that supports Qingxiao, she works best with Mornye but also makes good use of alternative Supports like Ciaccona and Shorekeeper, only having to deal with minimal team damage losses if Mornye is inaccessible/has to be replaced.
